title: Football transfer rumours: Chelsea to sign Giorgio Chiellini from Juventus?
trail: Phil Jones to Stoke? | West Ham in for Wilfried Bony? | Joe Hart off to Everton? | Jay Rodriguez set for West Brom move?
body: You suspect that getting on the wrong side of Antonio Conte would be bad news. The Mill reckons he knows that move where cold-blooded hitmen in films just chop the side of your neck and kill you – he doesn’t use it, but he’ll let you know it’s an option, just in case. With that in mind, we wouldn’t want to work in the Chelsea transfer team at the moment, with Conte supposedly irked that they haven’t bought him the players he wants. Perhaps with that fear of retribution in mind, it sounds like they might be pulling their collective fingers out and making a £25m bid for one Giorgio Chiellini. Sure, that’s a lot of money for an 82-year-old, or however old Chiellini is, but by crikey, what a sight it would be to have that noble beast in the Premier League. Manchester United, on the other hand, are seemingly a little more modest in their approach towards recruiting a new defender, which isn’t to say the man they have in mind won’t be as good. They’re still keen on Southampton’s José Fonte, as José Mourinho surveys the available central defensive options and decides they aren’t quite his tempo. Chris Smalling apparently fears this might hamper his England chances so is at least glancing towards the exit door with the corner of his eye, while if Phil Jones is released into the wild, Stoke City will be there to gather him in their arms and care for him. West Ham just about scraped a victory in their first league game at the new gaff on Sunday, but with assorted ailments both entirely predictable (Andy Carroll) and sightly less so (André Ayew), they could probably do with some help up top. Step forward Wilfried Bony, available from Manchester City and presumably willing to get the heck out of there. As sagas go, Arsenal chasing Shkodran Mustafi like they’re in a Benny Hill film is fairly tedious, and it looks like it will drag on for a little bit longer. Arsène Wenger reckons they are still discussing a deal, and that he hopes it’ll be done soon, but some reports claim it will set them back £50m. So will he baulk at breaking the club’s transfer record for someone who might turn out to be a third-choice centre-back, or will he hold his nose and do it? The tension is unbearable. And speaking of sagas, it seems Joe Hart’s move away from Manchester City depends very much on a chain of transfers coming off. City won’t let him go to Everton until Claudio Bravo arrives from Barcelona, but they won’t sell their man until they’ve signed Jasper Cillessen from Ajax. No word on whether the Dutch side will need to get a replacement in before they sell Cillessen, or whether the team they get that replacement from will need a replacement before they let the replacement go, or whether the team selling the replacement for the replacement will hold things up before they get a replacement of their own. Or something like that. Speaking of Everton (which we did somewhere in the middle there), they are busy finding ways to spend their new riches, and some of it might go on Porto midfielder Yacine Brahimi, a fine player in the Mill’s ‘umble opinion, which should obviously be the clincher in these things. Ronald, if you’re reading, don’t worry: we approve. Also, they’re similarly keen on a player the Mill doesn’t know much about, but we hope this won’t put them off their apparent chase for Lyon winger Rachid Ghezzal, who will cost something like £9m. Any other business? Well Jay Rodriguez looks like he’s set to do one from Southampton, with West Brom the most likely destination, but Hull are also keen. And if you fancy an update on Jay’s condition or movements, you know where to go. Should Lamine Koné leave Sunderland (and some people reckon the WANTAWAY defender has been BANNED from the club) they will make a £3m offer for Barnsley defender Alfie Mawson, and actually might do that anyway since David Moyes admitted they were a little light on defenders Juan Cuadrado should go back to Italy on loan this week, probably to Juventus. Inter are kicking the tyres of Newcastle’s Moussa Sissoko. And Atlético Madrid defender Javier Manquillo is wanted by Watford and Sunderland. There ends your serving of transfer gossip for the day. Peace be with you.
